section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Hyde Park (the first applicant) lobbied, among other things, for freedom of expression and the right to peaceful assembly.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: In 2007, Hyde Park's members decided to discontinue the organisation's registration with the Moldovan Ministry of Justice.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Hyde Park's members decided to discontinue the organisation's registration on grounds of alleged pressure and intimidation by the State.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Hyde Park's members complained of the refusal of the Moldovan Ministry of Justice to register amendments to Hyde Park's articles of association.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Hyde Park's members complained of the repeated freezing of Hyde Park's bank account.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Hyde Park's members complained of the arbitrary arrest of Hyde Park's members.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Hyde Park's members complained of attempts to shut down Hyde Park's newspaper.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Several of Hyde Park's leaders requested political asylum in western countries.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: It was decided to continue Hyde Park's activity under the same name but without registering it with the State authorities.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: It was decided that the new unincorporated association would become the former registered organisation Hyde Park's successor.

text: On 6 December 2004, Hyde Park applied to the Chişinău Municipal Council for authorisation to hold a peaceful meeting in front of the Romanian Embassy on 5 January 2005.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The purpose of the planned meeting on 5 January 2005 was to protest against the policy of Romania in respect of Moldovan students.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The application to the Chişinău Municipal Council was signed by Hyde Park's president.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Hyde Park's application to the Chişinău Municipal Council stated that members and supporters of Hyde Park who study in Romania or who have relatives studying there were not content with the manner in which they were treated by the Romanian authorities.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Hyde Park's application to the Chişinău Municipal Council stated that the intended protest would take place in front of the Romanian Embassy, between 11 a.m. and 2 p.m., in front of the entrance on Bucharest street.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Hyde Park's application to the Chişinău Municipal Council stated that Hyde Park undertook to respect public order and not to block traffic.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 30 December 2004, the Chişinău Municipal Council rejected Hyde Park's application to hold a protest meeting on 5 January 2005.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Chişinău Municipal Council rejected Hyde Park's application on the ground that the municipal police considered the applicants' protest to be unfounded and unwelcome.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Chişinău Municipal Council's rejection stated that it was the Government of Romania which financed the studies of Moldovan students in Romania and therefore the Romanian authorities were competent to take a decision in respect of the applicants' application of 6 December 2004.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 3 January 2005, Hyde Park (the first applicant) challenged the Chişinău Municipal Council's refusal in court.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Hyde Park (the first applicant) argued in court that the Chişinău Municipal Council's refusal was unlawful.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Hyde Park (the first applicant) argued that the Chişinău Municipal Council had protracted the examination of their application until the last day of the year so as not to leave it enough time to challenge the refusal in the courts.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Hyde Park (the first applicant) asked that the case be examined urgently.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Hyde Park (the first applicant) explained that many persons who had expressed their wish to participate in the demonstration were students in Romania and were at home, in Chişinău, only for the winter break.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 21 February 2005, the Chişinău Court of Appeal dismissed the applicants' action against the Chişinău Municipal Council's refusal to authorise the demonstration.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Chişinău Court of Appeal found on 21 February 2005 that the Chişinău Municipal Council had acted within its competence in refusing the demonstration.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Chişinău Court of Appeal observed that the police, the Prosecutor's Office and the Secret Service had obtained information that the applicants intended to breach the provisions of sections 6 and 7 of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Hyde Park appealed against the Chişinău Court of Appeal's judgment of 21 February 2005.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Hyde Park argued on appeal that the Chişinău Court of Appeal's judgment of 21 February 2005 had breached the right of Hyde Park's members to hold peaceful meetings in public places.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Hyde Park argued on appeal that no evidence had been presented to support the view that the holding of the demonstration would have given rise to an infringement of sections 6 and 7 of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 8 June 2005, the Supreme Court of Justice upheld Hyde Park's appeal against the Chişinău Court of Appeal's judgment of 21 February 2005.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 8 June 2005, the Supreme Court of Justice quashed the Chişinău Court of Appeal's judgment of 21 February 2005.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 8 June 2005, the Supreme Court of Justice ordered a re-examination of the case concerning Hyde Park's application to hold a demonstration in front of the Romanian Embassy.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Supreme Court of Justice found on 8 June 2005 that there was no evidence that the applicants intended to breach sections 6 and 7 of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 6 October 2005, the Chişinău Court of Appeal again dismissed the applicants' action concerning the refusal to authorise the demonstration in front of the Romanian Embassy.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Chişinău Court of Appeal dismissed the action on 6 October 2005 on the basis that the holding of a protest meeting in front of the Romanian Embassy could have prejudiced the image of the Moldovan State and of the Moldovan people.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Chişinău Court of Appeal found on 6 October 2005 that the decision to hold a protest meeting had not been adopted by the council of Hyde Park, as required by Hyde Park's statutes.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Chişinău Court of Appeal found on 6 October 2005 that Hyde Park's statutes did not contain, in its list of activities, provisions sanctioning actions such as holding protest meetings.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Hyde Park (the first applicant) appealed against the Chişinău Court of Appeal's judgment of 6 October 2005.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 14 December 2005, the Supreme Court of Justice dismissed the applicants' appeal on points of law against the Chişinău Court of Appeal's judgment of 6 October 2005.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Supreme Court of Justice dismissed the applicants' appeal on 14 December 2005 on the ground that the holding of a demonstration in front of the Romanian Embassy could have prejudiced the image of the Moldovan State and of the Moldovan people.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Section 6(1) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that assemblies shall be conducted peacefully, without any sort of weapons, and shall ensure the protection of participants and the environment, without impeding the normal use of public highways, road traffic and the operation of economic undertakings and without degenerating into acts of violence capable of endangering the public order and the physical integrity and life of persons or their property.

Section 7 of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that assemblies shall be suspended in the following circumstances: denial and defamation of the State and of the people; incitement to war or aggression and incitement to hatred on ethnic, racial or religious grounds; incitement to discrimination, territorial separatism or public violence; acts that undermine the constitutional order.

Section 8(1) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that assemblies may be conducted in squares, streets, parks and other public places in cities, towns and villages, and also in public buildings.

Section 8(2) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that it shall be forbidden to conduct an assembly in the buildings of the public authorities, the local authorities, prosecutors' offices, the courts or companies with armed security.

Section 8(3)(a) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that it shall be forbidden to conduct assemblies within fifty metres of the parliament building, the residence of the President of Moldova, the seat of the government, the Constitutional Court and the Supreme Court of Justice.

Section 8(3)(b) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that it shall be forbidden to conduct assemblies within twenty-five metres of the buildings of the central administrative authority, the local public authorities, courts, prosecutors' offices, police stations, prisons and social rehabilitation institutions, military installations, railway stations, airports, hospitals, companies which use dangerous equipment and machines, and diplomatic institutions.
Section 8(4) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that free access to the premises of the institutions listed in section 8(3) shall be guaranteed.
Section 8(5) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that the local public authorities may, if the organisers agree, establish places or buildings for permanent assemblies.

Section 11(1) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that not later than fifteen days prior to the date of the assembly, the organiser shall submit a notification to the Municipal Council, a specimen of which is set out in the annex which forms an integral part of the Act.

Section 11(2) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that the prior notification shall indicate: the name of the organiser and the aim of the assembly; the date, starting time and finishing time; the location and the access and return routes; the manner in which the assembly is to take place; the approximate number of participants; the persons who are to ensure and answer for the sound conduct of the assembly; and the services the organiser asks the Municipal Council to provide.

Section 11(3) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that if the situation so requires, the Municipal Council may alter certain aspects of the prior notification with the agreement of the organiser of the assembly.

Section 12(1) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that the prior notification shall be examined by the local government of the town or village at the latest 5 days before the date of the assembly.

Section 12(2) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that when the prior notification is considered at an ordinary or extraordinary meeting of the Municipal Council, the discussion shall deal with the form, timetable, location and other conditions for the conduct of the assembly and the decision taken shall take account of the specific situation.

Section 12(6) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that the local authorities can reject an application to hold an assembly only if after having consulted the police, it has obtained convincing evidence that the provisions of sections 6 and 7 will be breached with serious consequences for society.

Section 14(1) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that a decision rejecting the application for holding an assembly shall be reasoned and presented in writing and shall contain reasons for refusing to issue the authorisation.
Section 15(1) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that the organiser of the assembly can challenge the refusal in the administrative courts.
On 22 February 2008, the Parliament of Moldova adopted a new Assemblies Act.
The new Assemblies Act adopted on 22 February 2008 provides that no authorisation is needed for the holding of demonstrations with less than fifty participants.
